fields.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that provides:
fields.note: The ban, the exception and limits (a)-(c) all match Section 4. The closing sentence defining rent control as any regulation that in any way requires below-market rents appears nowhere in the document.

fields.quoted_span: nor may such regulation apply to any rental unit that is owned by a person or entity owning less than ten rental units or that has a fair market rent exceeding $400
fields.note: The summary also matches subsection (a), voluntary compliance after six months, and subsection (c), compensation from the municipality's general funds.
The field is null and the document gives no enactment or effective date.

fields.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind
fields.note: The present-tense statutory text is consistent with the provision being in force. The document never states its status, and the facts about the failed repeal petition are not in it.

fields.quoted_span: compliance on the part of property owners as to the rent control regulation or any subsequently adopted rent control regulation shall be entirely voluntary and uncoerced, and the property of a person or entity declining to have his or its property subjected to such regulation shall be wholly unaffected
fields.note: The ten-unit owner limit, the $400 fair market rent limit, the accepting-municipality condition and the preemptive effect are all stated in the text.

fields.quoted_span: General Law - Part I, Title VII, Chapter 40P, Section 4
fields.note: This matches the primary citation G.L. c. 40P, § 4. The aliases for §§ 2 and 3 are not in this document.
